question: What is Switzerland's current legal and operating perimeter for cryptoassets, stablecoins, ledger-based securities, custody, regulated DLT markets and tokenised central-bank settlement; what are the four systemically important banking groups and specialist crypto banks actually doing; and where do claim, reserve, finality, correction and loss remain?
bluf: Switzerland regulates crypto-related activity through existing functional financial-market perimeters plus the 2021 DLT legislation, not one general crypto licence. FINMA-authorised banks and securities firms, the regulated SIX digital securities infrastructure and the first DLT trading facility supply named institutional entry points. The SNB has issued wholesale CBDC for live production-environment settlement on SIX since December 2023 and extended the bounded Helvetia pilot through at least June 2028; BX Digital separately uses a production SIC RTGS link with traditional central-bank money. All four systemically important banking groups participate in the controlled CHFD stablecoin sandbox, but they do not thereby become issuers: Swiss Stablecoin AG provides issuance infrastructure and CHFD Infrastruktur AG operates the platform. Separately, UBS has live tokenised-securities and fund workflows but no active spot-crypto offer on its cited product page; ZKB directly custodies bitcoin and ether while Crypto Finance executes trades; PostFinance offers 22-asset trading, custody and ETH staking with Sygnum; and no broader Raiffeisen customer crypto product was verified. Stablecoins remain private repayment claims and the sandbox is not a public launch. No permanent CBDC, retail CBDC or recurring cross-border route is established, so the map carries no route arc.

authority.summary: The Confederation defines the Swiss franc; the SNB owns central-bank money, SIC rules and payment-system oversight; FINMA owns prudential, conduct and FMI licensing; FINMA-recognised SROs supervise many AML-only financial intermediaries; tax, courts and insolvency authorities retain separate roles. The 2021 DLT Act adapted existing law rather than creating a single crypto regulator.
authority.boundary: Currency, prudential licence, conduct, AML membership, market-infrastructure approval, tax, adjudication and insolvency distribution are separate authorities and states.

legal_objects.summary: The record separates coins and banknotes, SNB sight deposits, commercial-bank deposits, Helvetia wholesale CBDC as a technical representation of SNB sight deposits, payment tokens, utility tokens, asset tokens, ledger-based securities, stablecoin issuer claims, custodied cryptobased assets and settlement entries. Hybrid-token rules may be cumulative.
legal_objects.boundary: A shared token or ledger form does not merge sovereign money, bank liability, issuer debt, investment right, custody asset, securities record or final cash settlement.

permitted_activities.summary: Payment, exchange, custody, deposit-taking, securities dealing, asset management, fund activity and FMI operation are permitted only through their applicable AML, fintech, bank, securities, financial-service, collective-investment or infrastructure rules. DLT facilities may conduct qualifying multilateral DLT-securities trading and specified custody or clearing/settlement functions. The proposed dedicated payment-instrument and crypto-institution categories are not current law at the cutoff.
permitted_activities.boundary: Technology, marketing, token issuance, SRO membership and one licence category do not authorize all services or instruments.

entry_gates.summary: Professional AML-covered intermediaries require direct supervision or recognised-SRO membership. Current fintech authorisation covers up to CHF 100 million of public deposits or collective cryptobased-asset custody if assets are neither invested nor interest-bearing; larger or invested deposits enter the banking perimeter. Securities, funds and FMIs have distinct gates. DLT trading facilities require FINMA authorisation before operation.
entry_gates.boundary: Application, SRO affiliation, licence, licence effectiveness, product admission, launch, first transaction and recurring production each need separate evidence.

named_operating_actors.summary: FINMA's current material names UBS, Raiffeisen Group, Zürcher Kantonalbank and PostFinance as systemically important. The authorised-institutions list separately names AMINA Bank AG and Sygnum Bank AG as banks and Crypto Finance AG and Taurus SA as securities firms. All four systemic groups participate in the controlled CHFD sandbox, while customer-product states differ: ZKB provides direct bitcoin/ether custody and an interbank service; PostFinance offers 22-asset trading, custody and ETH staking with Sygnum; UBS operates tokenised-asset workflows but its cited service page says it has no active crypto offering; and no broader Raiffeisen customer crypto launch was verified. SIX operates regulated digital-securities CSD infrastructure; BX Digital is the sole listed DLT trading facility. Nine banks are currently eligible for Helvetia wCBDC, but eligibility does not establish usage by each bank.
named_operating_actors.boundary: Legal person, group, ordinary licence, crypto-facing service, product admission, technical connection and active transaction are distinct facts.

claims_and_backing.summary: FINMA says stablecoin holders generally hold an at-any-time payment claim against the issuer; classification normally follows public-deposit or collective-investment law depending on whose account and risk the backing is managed for. A bank default guarantee can remove funds from the deposit definition but carries conditions and residual issuer, holder and guarantor risks. The sandbox describes CHFD as 1:1 CHF-linked but does not publish the complete debtor, reserve, guarantee, redemption, attestation or insolvency chain. The participating banks are not automatically co-issuers. Helvetia wCBDC is an SNB liability; commercial deposits and custodied cryptoassets follow different protection paths.
claims_and_backing.boundary: Legal design, guarantee, reserve asset, dated balance, attestation, liquidity, redemption request, completed payment, deposit insurance and insolvency recovery are separate evidence states.

domestic_rails.summary: SIC is the sovereign Swiss-franc RTGS and finality anchor, operated by SIX Interbank Clearing under SNB rules. SIC instant payments provide 24/7 final account-to-account settlement. SIX supplies regulated tokenised-securities issuance and post-trade services; Helvetia supplies integrated wCBDC DvP on the SIX platform; BX Digital uses a synchronised Ethereum/SIC RTGS link with traditional SNB money.
domestic_rails.boundary: Crypto transfer, securities-ledger transfer, custody book, wCBDC movement, commercial-bank customer credit and SIC final settlement are distinct records and clocks.

cross_border_routes.summary: Project Jura concluded after near-real real-value CHF/EUR wholesale-CBDC and tokenised-commercial-paper transactions. Project Agorá conducted 30 controlled real-value transactions across 17 multinational scenarios in July 2026, with total value about CHF 800,000 and no integration as a recurring production corridor. The SNB-ECB instant-payment link remained a feasibility assessment.
cross_border_routes.boundary: Real-value experiment, prototype, feasibility study and production corridor are different states; no bilateral map arc is authorised.

operating_state.summary: The DLT legal framework, SDX/CSD infrastructure, SIC and instant payments are effective and operational. Helvetia wCBDC has been used for live production-environment settlement since December 2023 and now runs through at least June 2028 as a pilot. BX Digital holds an effective licence and the SNB describes its RTGS link as productive. CHFD became technically live inside a controlled sandbox at the end of June 2026 and entered a nine-company use-case test phase on 8 September; the test has restricted participants and limits and is not a public product or market decision. Dedicated stablecoin and crypto-institution licences remain proposed, and no retail or permanent wholesale CBDC is established.
operating_state.boundary: Effective law, licence, technical readiness, production connection, bounded pilot, first transaction, recurring operation and permanent policy adoption are not interchangeable.

scale.summary: SIX reports more than CHF 2 billion of securities issued through SDX. The initial Helvetia phase involved six banks, six digital-bond issuances and about CHF 750 million of settled transaction value; the SNB also issued CHF 64 million of digital SNB Bills. Nine banks are currently wCBDC-eligible. SIC settled 1.0 billion transactions in 2025, averaging 4.1 million and CHF 220 billion daily. Agorá's controlled test totalled about CHF 800,000. ZKB reported CHF 55 million of cryptobased client assets for 2025, up from CHF 19 million, while PostFinance disclosed 22 supported cryptoassets but no balance or transaction series. CHFD supplied neither circulation nor reserve amounts.
scale.boundary: Issued securities, pilot settlement, eligible participants, whole-rail fiat volume and controlled-test value have different populations and do not measure national crypto adoption.

stress.summary: FINMA's final X AG case records an observed stablecoin guarantee failure: one of two bank guarantees fell away, full repayment was no longer assured and the issuer unlawfully accepted public deposits. FINMA's custody guidance identifies technology, concentration, foreign-law, subcustodian and insolvency risks. No joined national customer-loss or recovery series was located.
stress.boundary: Risk warning, guarantee loss, unlawful deposit-taking, licence action, actual shortfall, customer loss, adjudication and restitution are separate facts.

correction_and_loss.summary: Correction may occur through issuer redemption or balance-sheet repair, chain or securities-ledger action, custodian and CSD records, SIC payment processes, FINMA restoration or licence measures, and court or insolvency adjudication. Qualifying custody assets can be segregated; bank deposits have a separate CHF 100,000 protection structure; present fintech funds are not privileged or deposit-insured. SIC settlement is final and irrevocable in central-bank money.
correction_and_loss.boundary: Technical reversal, compensating transfer, segregation, deposit payout, regulatory restoration, court claim and final cash settlement have separate clocks.

evidence_boundary.summary: The recertification uses current FINMA, SNB, SIF, Federal Council, tax-authority, SIX, BIS and bank materials and retains four existing Workbench owners as bounded context. It adds the four-systemic-bank comparison and the omitted live-but-controlled CHFD test state, resolves the June 2028 Helvetia horizon and productive BX RTGS-link state, and carries zero route arcs. No post-15 September crypto operating-state change was found through the intraday cutoff.
evidence_boundary.boundary: Fresh research is not Chronicle promotion, publication authority, investment advice, watch creation, app shipment, permission to edit generated files or proof of a recurring crypto corridor.
